4

6	REPO="gastownhall/beads"
7	METHOD="squash"
8	FLAKE_RERUN="allowed"
9	PR=""
10	BEAD_OVERRIDE=""
11

13	  echo "usage: pr-handoff <pr-number> [--repo owner/repo] [--method squash|merge|rebase] [--no-flake-rerun] [--bead <id>]" >&2
14	}
15

17	  case "$1" in
18	    --repo)
19	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
20	      REPO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
21	    --method)
22	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
23	      METHOD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
24	    --bead)
25	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
26	      BEAD_OVERRIDE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
27	    --no-flake-rerun) FLAKE_RERUN="no"; shift ;;
28	    -*) usage; exit 2 ;;
29	    *)
30	      [[ -z "$PR" ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
31	      PR="$1"; shift ;;
32	  esac
33	done
34	
35	[[ "$PR" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
36	[[ "$REPO" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
37	[[ "$METHOD" =~ ^(squash|merge|rebase)$ ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
38	[[ -z "$BEAD_OVERRIDE" || "$BEAD_OVERRIDE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
39	
40	cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
41	pr_json="$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json title,state 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "cannot read PR" >&2; exit 1; }

44

46	legacy="gh-pr-$PR"
47	if [[ -n "$BEAD_OVERRIDE" ]]; then
48	  bead="$BEAD_OVERRIDE"
49	  selected="$(bd show "$bead" --json 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "cannot inspect bead $bead" >&2; exit 1; }
50	  selected_ref="$(jq -er '.[0].external_ref // ""' <<<"$selected")" || { echo "malformed bead $bead" >&2; exit 1; }
51	  if [[ -n "$selected_ref" && "$selected_ref" != "$canonical" && ! ( "$REPO" == "gastownhall/beads" && "$selected_ref" == "$legacy" ) ]]; then
52	    echo "bead $bead belongs to $selected_ref, not $canonical" >&2

54	  fi

58	    matches+=$'\n'"$(bd list --json --external-ref "$legacy" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].id // empty')"
59	  fi
60	  matches="$(sort -u <<<"$matches" | sed '/^$/d')"
61	  match_count="$(wc -l <<<"$matches" | tr -d ' ')"
62	  (( match_count <= 1 )) || { echo "ambiguous merge-tail beads for $canonical" >&2; exit 1; }
63	  bead="$matches"
64	fi
65	
66	if [[ -z "$bead" ]]; then

68	  [[ -n "$bead" ]] || exit 1
69	fi
70	
71	bd update "$bead" --claim --add-label merge-when-green --external-ref "$canonical" \
72	  --set-metadata "pr_babysit_repo=$REPO" \
73	  --set-metadata "pr_babysit_pr=$PR" \
74	  --set-metadata "pr_babysit_method=$METHOD" \
75	  --set-metadata "pr_babysit_flake_rerun=$FLAKE_RERUN" \
76	  --set-metadata pr_babysit_last_transition= \
77	  --append-notes "[pr-handoff $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] repo=$REPO pr=$PR method=$METHOD flake_rerun=$FLAKE_RERUN — patrol owns the merge; sessions hand off here." \
78	  >/dev/null
79	
80	echo "handed off: $REPO#$PR -> bead $bead"
81	if ! systemctl --user is-active --quiet pr-babysit.timer 2>/dev/null; then
82	  echo "WARNING: pr-babysit.timer is not active. Enable with: scripts/install-pr-babysit" >&2
83	fi

# Review: pr-babysit merge-tail patrol series (mybd main, `d5d4355` → `1e33d26`)

## Overview

This series landed as five direct commits on main (no PR): the initial patrol (`d5d4355`, Fable), then four hardening rounds signed `codex-gpt-5.6-terra-high`. Net result:

- **`scripts/pr-babysit`** — a zero-token systemd-timer patrol that owns "merge when green" PR tails: reads `merge-when-green` beads, validates PR identity and policy, waits on pending checks, spends a one-per-head flake-rerun budget, runs a blocking `pr-preflight` base-health check, then merges with `--match-head-commit` CAS and closes the bead only after confirming `MERGED`.
- **`scripts/pr-handoff`** — session-side handoff: finds/creates the bead, writes namespaced `pr_babysit_*` metadata, labels it, warns if the timer isn't active.
- **`scripts/install-pr-babysit`** + systemd units — installer that resolves the stable checkout (worktree-aware via `--git-common-dir`), validates the path for systemd-unsafe characters, and verifies the generated unit.
- **`scripts/test-pr-babysit`** — ~35 hermetic behavioral tests with fake `gh`/`bd`/preflight.
- AGENTS.md documents the role split (sessions produce, only the patrol merges) motivated by the beads#4942 red-nix collision.

## What I verified empirically

- **Test suite passes** on this machine.
- **`gh pr checks --json` exits 0 even with failing checks** (tested against gastownhall/beads#4929, which has 2 failing checks). This was my top suspicion — the fake `gh` defaults `FAKE_CHECKS_EXIT=0`, and without `--json` the real command exits non-zero on fail/pending, which would have dead-ended the rerun/block paths at the `checks-unavailable` transition. Reality matches the fake; **no bug**.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array** with `.[0]` shape as the patrol assumes; `bd list --label merge-when-green --json` returns a clean array.
- The jq run-id capture expression (`capture(...)?.id // empty`, `pr-babysit:140`) parses and extracts correctly, including for empty links.

## Strengths

This is unusually careful bash for an auto-merge bot. The safety ladder is genuinely fail-closed at every rung: malformed queue data, malformed metadata, identity mismatches (external_ref vs metadata vs legacy note), invalid policy, gh non-zero status *even with valid JSON*, unknown check buckets, empty check lists, preflight exit-zero-without-explicit-green, head drift between checks and merge, merge-queued-but-not-merged, and bead-authorization revocation re-read immediately before the merge (`pr-babysit:178`). The rerun budget is reserved *before* calling GitHub so a crash conservatively spends it (`pr-babysit:142-144`). Transitions are idempotent across timer firings so bead notes don't grow unboundedly. The distinction between `transition` (retain under patrol, retry forever) and `block` (unclaim + relabel for agent judgment) is applied thoughtfully — notably red-base retains while other preflight blocks escalate.

## Findings

None are merge-blocking; the design bias is conservative throughout, so the failure modes below are livelocks or noise, not bad merges.

**1. Silent livelock on the pre-merge authorization CAS — `scripts/pr-babysit:178-181` (low-medium, observability).**
The CAS requires `bd show` output to deep-equal the queue snapshot (`status`, `assignee`, `external_ref`, `notes`, `metadata`). If `bd list` and `bd show` ever serialize a field differently (e.g. one omits an empty `assignee`, the other emits `""` — I confirmed `bd show` *omits* absent fields), every merge attempt skips with only a local `log` line. Unlike every other retained state, this path writes **no transition to the bead**, so a persistent mismatch is invisible to agents running `bd ready` — the bead just sits green and unmerged forever, and only `patrol.log` knows why. Suggest: after N consecutive CAS skips for the same head, write a `transition` (or at least log a distinctive escalating marker) so the failure surfaces on the bead.

**2. Note growth for long-pending PRs — `scripts/pr-babysit:134`.**
The `waiting:$head:$pending:$failing` key embeds live counts, so a PR whose pending count ticks down 10→0 appends up to ~10 notes per head, and again per push. Idempotency only holds for an *unchanged* count. Cheap fix: drop `$pending:$failing` from the key (keep them in the message text).

**3. Stale comment — `scripts/pr-babysit:42-44`.**
`legacy_policy` says "Output method<TAB>rerun" but emits `repo<TAB>pr<TAB>method<TAB>rerun`. The callers use all four fields correctly; only the comment is wrong.

**4. Test-coverage gaps (minor).**
Untested paths: already-`MERGED` at first read closes the bead (`pr-babysit:116-119`); `CLOSED`-unmerged removes the label (`:120-123`); patrol-side resolution of the legacy `gh-pr-N` external_ref (`:68-69` — only the handoff side of legacy refs is tested); partial rerun success (some `gh run rerun` calls fail, one succeeds). Given how much this suite already covers, these are polish.

**5. `statusCheckRollup` truncation risk — `scripts/pr-babysit:172` (informational).**
GraphQL rollup fields can paginate on PRs with very many checks; beads#4929 has 71 and returned fully, so this is theoretical at current scale — and truncation would fail toward "not all green," i.e. conservative.

**6. Machine-specific PATH baked into the unit — `scripts/systemd/pr-babysit.service`.**
`/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` is hardcoded. Fine for a personal repo, but if the timer is ever installed on the Windows/other machines mentioned in AGENTS.md, `bd`/`gh` resolution silently degrades to "bd unavailable; skipping" — which at least fails closed and logs.

## Conventions & security

- Follows repo conventions: bash scripts, extensionless, agent-signed commits, AGENTS.md policy documented alongside the mechanism, `PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE=1` per the stop-the-line rule.
- Injection surface is well-guarded: `repo`/`pr`/`method`/`rerun` are all regex-validated before reaching `gh` argv (`pr-babysit:47,96,102`; `pr-handoff:35-38`); bead notes (agent-writable) are only pattern-matched, never executed; the installer rejects systemd-metacharacter paths and escapes the sed replacement.
- One deliberate and correct choice worth calling out: the *only* authority to merge is the conjunction of bead label + valid policy + green checks + green base + unchanged head — no prose is trusted (`legacy_policy` requires the exact machine-written marker line, and mismatched legacy identity blocks).

## Verdict

Solid merge. The one change I'd actually make is finding 1 (surface persistent CAS skips on the bead); 2 and 3 are trivial cleanups to batch with it. Nothing here needs a revert or urgent follow-up — the failure modes are all "doesn't merge and tells you quietly," never "merges wrongly."

Done — everything is landed and synced. Here's the summary:

## Review recorded and fixes applied

- **Review record**: appended to `mybd-nfrv` ("Harden pr-babysit into a fail-closed merge controller"), the bead that drove the series.
- **Fixes**: committed on a worktree branch and fast-forwarded to main as `88f3fafd4`, pushed. The live timer runs from this checkout, so the patrol is already using them.
  - The pre-merge authorization skip now writes a once-per-head `authorization-mismatch` transition to the bead instead of only the local patrol log, so a persistent mismatch can't livelock invisibly.
  - The `waiting` transition key no longer embeds pending/failing counts (they moved into the message), so bead notes stop growing as counts tick down.
  - Fixed the stale `legacy_policy` comment, and added five tests covering the previously untested paths (MERGED-at-first-read, CLOSED-unmerged, patrol-side legacy `gh-pr-N` resolution, changing-count idempotency, mismatch surfacing).
- **Gates**: `bash -n`, ShellCheck clean, full hermetic suite PASS. `bd dolt push` and `git push` both succeeded.

## Porting assessment: not worth it — designate one babysitter

Your instinct is right, and there's already a bead for this (`mybd-jgxt`, "Port pr-babysit to Windows"); I appended this assessment to it rather than re-scoping it without you.

**Why a port loses on architecture, not just effort:** the patrol is a singleton controller. Bead state syncs by *manual* `bd dolt push/pull`, so a second patrol machine would read a stale queue, and its rerun-budget and transition writes would be invisible to the first machine until the next sync. Two patrols means split-brain flake-rerun budgets and concurrent Dolt writes — exactly what this repo's "keep bd serial" rule exists to prevent. The GitHub-side `--match-head-commit` CAS makes a double *merge* harmless, but nothing prevents a double *rerun*. One babysitter is also the auditable design: one actor merges, one log to read.

**Why a language port buys little anyway:** `gh` and `bd` stay external CLIs in any language, so a Go/Python/Rust version is the same shell-out orchestration in different syntax. The actual asset is the tested fail-closed decision ladder plus its ~40-case hermetic test suite — all of which would need reimplementing and re-verifying (days of work) to gain nothing the single-babysitter design doesn't already give you.

**What Windows actually needs** is only the enqueue path, and `pr-handoff` already runs under Git Bash (no `flock`, no systemd dependency except a warning). The residual work, if you re-scope `mybd-jgxt`, is small:

1. Make the handoff's timer warning platform-aware — on a non-systemd host it should say "the babysitter is the Linux machine," not "your timer is inactive."
2. Close the sync gap: Windows session-close already mandates `bd dolt push`, but the Linux babysitter needs a periodic `bd dolt pull` (as a patrol pre-step or a sibling timer) or cross-machine handoffs sit unseen until your next manual pull. This is the one genuinely missing piece.
3. Document the designation in AGENTS.md "PR Merge Tails."

If the Linux box ever proves unreliable for days at a time, the fallback is the already-policy-allowed in-session merge on decisively-green PRs — and only then would a port (Go, as a single binary) be worth revisiting.
